steps.what: Discuss funeral, burial or cremation wishes and practical constraints with the authorised family representative
Check funeral service times, locations and floral delivery availability
Write the funeral plan and supplier booking requests with selected details
outputs: final funeral plan and request drafts

steps.what: Confirm the final funeral plan details and cost with the authorised family representative
inputs: final funeral plan and request drafts

steps.what: Check the family-approved funeral requests against availability and exact supplier recipients
Send the approved funeral, burial or cremation booking requests to the named suppliers

tasks.design: Configure availability views and the existing funeral-case plan template in {OPS_SYSTEM}, using {CALENDAR} for recorded slots. Capture the family's choices once, then obtain confirmation of the finished plan and check supplier details before the separate request send through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparing recorded availability and repeating the same service details in requests consumes coordination time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case forms can reuse names, times and locations across the actual plan and booking requests.
tasks.still_hard: Family wishes, cultural requirements and supplier availability that has changed since the last update.
tasks.human_edge: Support difficult choices without rushing the family.

ambition.what: Check a family's preferred ceremony time against all recorded service constraints before proposing it.

reach.learn: Venue, transport and floral timing dependencies.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: case templates and availability views can reuse funeral arrangement details; family choices and supplier confirmation require personal coordination.

assumptions: Boundary covers the real plan and outgoing booking requests; supplier acceptance and delivery remain unchanged outside labour. These requests may contain several supplier-specific messages, each sent only from its approved content and recipient snapshot.

Family supplies wishes in s1. Existing coordinator or supplier updates provide venue, slot, delivery window and availability timestamp. Missing or stale availability requires calls in retained s2 time. Arranger captures deceased identifier, authorised representative, chosen service, times, locations and supplier instructions in s3.

Test native case templates first. S2 removes cross-view comparison only; s3 removes repeated field copying while retaining choice capture and custom wishes. Internal plan saves and the tiny manual send earn no saving.

Finished plan and requests exist before family confirmation in s4; arranger s5 validates readiness without changing content. Both approvals bind the exact requests and recipients in s6. Any change returns for the affected checks, including renewed family approval if their plan changes.

Focal baseline is 95 shares; five customer shares are excluded from savings. All times are illustrative and unmeasured. Family confirmation is existing work, not new free labour. Incremental upkeep covers availability/template corrections.
unknowns: Current availability freshness and existing case-template reuse.
research_questions: Which service details are actually re-entered across requests today?

already_counted.description: Conversation, stale-availability calls, choice capture, final checks and send remain.
Existing family plan confirmation remains outside the focal denominator.

incremental.description: Maintain case-template fields and repair stale availability links.

approvals.approved_version: family-confirmed s4 plan and final request content with exact supplier recipients checked in s5; missing family confirmation blocks release and any edit voids it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal B95, R74 gives gross 22.105 and net 21.105 after upkeep. Cautious case: mainly telephone availability leaves s2 at 85% and bespoke wishes leave s3 at 85%; focal gross is 7.105 and net 6.105, above low 5. Family and physical supplier labour are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Close the casket and lead the cortege

steps.what: Check the funeral instructions and route to churches or burial sites
Close caskets at the agreed point in the farewell
Lead funeral corteges to churches or burial sites with the mourners

tasks.design: Read the existing service instruction view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, then perform the casket closure and cortege leadership in person. The native instruction view is already adequate; no extra administrative record or route saving is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling and ceremonial leadership define this work.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability changes those actions in this design.
tasks.still_hard: Dignity, timing, safety and unexpected distress.
tasks.human_edge: Respond sensitively at the moment of farewell.

ambition.what: No increased ceremonial workload is assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: casket closure and leading a funeral cortege are physical ceremonial duties.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual instruction check, casket closure and cortege, not arranging the funeral. No closure log or trip report is invented.
Existing service coordinator supplies final destination, route, timing and family farewell instructions. Reading and resolving any ambiguity stays in s1. No new capture contract is needed.
Native service view is tested and assumed already adequate; its small check remains fully retained. Existing navigation runtime creates no saving, and travel reduction is not evidenced.
All shares are focal labour estimates; other attendants' work is unchanged. No new helper or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Whether the final instructions are already in one view.
research_questions: Does any actual repeated instruction lookup remain after checking the native service view?

already_counted.description: Instruction check and all physical ceremonial work remain.

incremental.description: No new helper or maintenance process.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Separate instruction lookup, casket handling and cortege leadership each retain their actual work. The existing view offers no additional change and no artificial record is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain funeral options and maintain the display

steps.what: Retrieve current funeral service options, products and merchandise prices
Provide information on funeral service options, products or merchandise in the family conversation
Maintain a casket display area by cleaning, arranging and checking the displayed merchandise

tasks.design: Configure a service and merchandise view in {OPS_SYSTEM} showing current prices and included elements. The arranger explains these to the family and continues to maintain the physical casket display; no choice or new sales record is inferred from a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparing several catalogue pages interrupts explanations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue filters can present the relevant current options together.
tasks.still_hard: Explain inclusions, exclusions and alternatives without pressuring a bereaved family.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the family needs time rather than another option.

ambition.what: No change in family decision authority is proposed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native catalogue views can reduce retrieval of current service prices; explanation and physical display maintenance remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes current-option lookup, explanation and physical display maintenance as stated. Actual booking choices are recorded in the separate arrangement workflow; no new information-session log is invented.

Existing catalogue owner supplies item id, service description, price, included elements, exclusions and validity. Arranger supplies the family question and checks relevance in s1. Missing or stale entries require manual confirmation within retained time.
Native catalogue views are tested first. The cut removes repeated page navigation only; all family discussion, cleaning, physical arrangement and label inspection remain.
All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates. Catalogue ownership and family decision time remain unchanged outside the denominator. Incremental allowance covers view and link corrections.
unknowns: Whether the catalogue already exposes comparable prices and inclusions in one view.
research_questions: Which actual questions require repeated catalogue navigation today?

already_counted.description: Option suitability checks, family explanation and physical display work remain.

incremental.description: Check saved catalogue views after price or product changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central catalogue cut 7 less upkeep 0.5 gives 6.5. Cautious case: exclusions lack structured fields so s1 retains 80%, giving 2 gross and 1.5 net, above low 1. Conversation and display care remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the family's stated wishes and relevant service context before offering counsel and comfort
Offer counsel and comfort to bereaved families or friends through listening and personal support

tasks.design: Use the existing family-context view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, then offer counsel and comfort in person. Its lookup is already short and the necessary reading remains; no automated condolence text or new counselling record is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attentive presence and sensitive listening are the work itself.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability changes this interaction in the proposed design.
tasks.still_hard: Respond to grief without assuming what a person needs.
tasks.human_edge: Be present, listen and recognise distress requiring specialist support.

ambition.what: No increase in bereavement conversation throughput is assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: personal bereavement support depends on responsive listening, while an existing case view can already provide the limited factual context.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual context check and bereavement support conversation. The arranger is not delivering clinical therapy. A service change or specialist referral, if requested, enters its existing separate action workflow and is not silently automated here.

Existing arrangement staff capture family wishes and service context during arrangements. The arranger reads those fields in s1; source interpretation remains, and no new recording, transcript or progress note is assumed for this support interaction.

Test native case view first; it already presents the necessary context, so a template removes no work. The separate lookup is fully retained, as is the conversation. No saving from existing system runtime is counted.
All shares are focal labour estimates. No additional helper or ongoing upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Whether the native family-context view is already adequate.
research_questions: Is there any actual repeated retrieval beyond necessary reading in the context check?

already_counted.description: Context reading and all personal support remain.

incremental.description: No new helper or maintenance process.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The actual lookup is split out and tested against the already adequate native view; its necessary reading and the entire comfort conversation stay unchanged. No unused counselling log is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The arranger retains family support and ceremonial duties while reusing reliable arrangement and catalogue details.
reach: Funeral service coordinator: prepare consistent booking requests from a confirmed plan.
role.ambitious_version: Offer families feasible arrangement choices with consistent supplier requests while preserving unhurried personal care.
